queue.done_note: Iteration 2 (2026-08-17T19:43+01:00): was a real bug, not a styling gap -- see the log's 19:43 entry. A1's Archive button transitions document.phase to archived but never relocates the file, while specNavigation.ts's isArchived() checked ONLY the path prefix spec/changes/archive/. A phase-archived document was invisible to the tree, the picker's Archived group, and the document panel's own header badge -- full opacity, grouped as current, indistinguishable from an approved document. Fixed at the source: /project/specs now joins the on-disk tree against each path's DB phase (spec_lifecycle.list_documents) and reports it; specNavigation.ts's isArchived(path, phase) returns true on either signal, so every consumer of SpecNode.archived is correct for both archiving mechanisms without being touched itself. Archived rows also get a distinct archive-box icon (added to Icon.tsx) and reduced opacity in SpecTree.tsx and SpecDocumentPicker.tsx. The fix surfaced (did not introduce) a second gap: a project whose only documents are all archived left SpecPage.tsx stuck on 'Loading...' forever (resolveSelection had nothing to hand back); added an explicit empty state. Verified live: screenshotted the seeded fixture before (bug visible) and after (icon + dim + correct grouping) in both themes via scripts/taste_shots.py, plus opened the document directly to confirm the header's Archived pill. Backend 92 tests green (hub/tests/test_spec*.py), frontend 961/961, lint clean, tsc clean. Committed 92ea5d6, pushed.

known_debts: The test fixture's StaticPool shares ONE sqlite connection across every session in the process, so any concurrent session can roll back another's pending write. Proven: 105/200 commits lost with a concurrent poller vs 0/200 without. test_a_conversation_whose_model_changed_attributes_usage_per_turn is xfailed because of it. A file-backed DATABASE_URL is NOT a drop-in fix -- it HUNG the suite when tried; it needs WAL plus a busy timeout.

The hub suite is ~100% fixture overhead: create_app() 121ms + drop_all/create_all across 43 tables 88ms = ~240ms per test x 2130 = ~510s against 477s observed. Session-scoping the app and schema would take it from 8 minutes to about 1.
